chap: Who uses hydrogen, and how clean is it?

cap: The world used 102 Mt of hydrogen in 2025. Only 0.88 Mt, less than 1%, was made with low emissions.
Switch to production: natural gas and coal still make almost all of it, emitting about 1,000 Mt of CO₂ a year.
But the clean side is moving fast: installed electrolysis grew +114% in 2025.

chap: Which countries felt the 2026 fertiliser shock?

cap: Brazil imports all the urea it uses, 40% from the Middle East. When Hormuz closed, its urea price rose 60% in a month.
Search any country. Morocco and South Korea import 100% of their ammonia.
27.9 Mt of clean hydrogen is promised for 2030. Only 4.4 Mt is committed, and 1.1 Mt is running.
The clock is ticking: 22 Mt may never start by 2030 without investment decisions by early 2027.
China leads with 2.7 GW of electrolysers. In 2026, Europe is set to roughly quadruple.
Factories could already build 6.4× what projects need. The missing piece is not supply. It is buyers.

chap: How far is clean hydrogen from competing?

cap: Renewable hydrogen costs from over USD 3 to beyond USD 10 per kg, against about USD 1 to 4 for natural gas.
The world's largest urea importer, a USD 58 bn industrial plan with 44 hydrogen projects selected, and 4.4 Mt announced in Latin America.
